threats.name: Use After Free
threats.rationale: Lua frees objects with a garbage collector and gives the program no deallocator or pointer, so use after free needs a native extension (a C rock, package.loadlib), a binary chunk or debug.* upvalue surgery; the library uses none by reading. The only finalizer-like hooks (__gc, __close) are not defined by the package.

threats.rationale: The Lua analogue of the class is indexing nil, which raises a catchable runtime error (not undefined behaviour) with a free-text message. The library avoids it on caller data: every container is type-checked before indexing (sequential.lua:72-82, :85-100, :420-440) and a missing field reaches check_bit as nil and is rejected as INVALID_BIT. Residual: the free-text nil-index error would be a different error class from the contract if some path indexed an unchecked value (none found by reading).

threats.name: Integer Overflow to Buffer Boundary
threats.rationale: Lua 5.4 integers are 64-bit and wrap silently on overflow; the registry class is the narrow one (a wrapped size or offset reaching a buffer). The library does no arithmetic on a caller value: widths are bounded to 65536 and 64 before use (sequential.lua:59-70) and the indices are loop counters. The size-explosion variant (a caller-sized allocation) is lua.unbounded-variadic-and-allocation. A float width is rejected by the integer-subtype check, so 2^53+1 cannot round.

closed_by.detail: No arithmetic, bitwise or comparison operator applies to a caller-supplied value before the integer-subtype guard; the only arithmetic is on loop indices bounded by the width caps (sequential.lua:181-205, :450-462). threats.name: rawlen on a table with holes silently picks a border
threats.rationale: The length of a Lua table with holes is any border, so rawlen({1, nil, 1}) may be 3 or 1 and the library then trusts it. The same trust is in check_ff_list (sequential.lua:85-100), Register (:296-305), ShiftRegister and Counter bits (:420-440, which compares rawlen to width but not the key set). The result is a wrong-length output rather than memory corruption, and it differs between Lua implementations and versions (LuaJIT, 5.1-5.5), so the lane is order- and version-dependent. Version note: the constructor form {1, nil, 1} truncates on Lua 5.5.0 only; on 5.4.7 (the CI interpreter) # is 3 and the following rawget raises INVALID_BIT, so CI would not see that probe. The hash-built form {[1]=1,[3]=1} truncates on both. The behaviour is implementation-defined, which ties this row to lua.interpreter-variance.

threats.name: error tables are mutable and forgeable
threats.rationale: The coded errors are plain mutable tables whose identity is "metatable == the private InvalidBit table and raw code == INVALID_BIT" (gates.lua:120-165). A caller who obtains one real error through getmetatable(err) can mint a table with the same metatable that is_invalid_bit accepts (probed: a forged table passed), and a handler can mutate err.code on a genuine error so the predicate then fails (probed: after err.code = "OTHER" the predicate returned false). Impact: a consumer that trusts is_invalid_bit for control flow can be steered by an attacker who controls objects passed through the error path; low severity for a gate library, but the identity contract is stronger than what is enforced. Three more routes, all probed on Lua 5.5.0: gates.raise_invalid_width and gates.raise_invalid_shape are public (gates.lua:169-176, exported through the gates module) and mint genuine errors from any text a caller supplies; err.value and err.param are mutable fields that the __tostring formatters print with %s (gates.lua:96-97, :102-103, :136-137, :142-143), so a caller who sets err.value to a table with __tostring makes tostring(err) run caller code (probed: "got CALLER CODE RAN"); and the predicates trust the metatable only. Fix: internal-only raisers, read-only error objects, a private registry of genuine instances.

closed_by.detail: Errors are tables with a stable code: INVALID_BIT, INVALID_ARITY, INVALID_WIDTH, INVALID_SHAPE (gates.lua:91-176), raised with error(t, 0) so no position prefix is added (:192, :201, :170, :175); predicates is_invalid_bit/arity/width/shape and error_code (:120-165) check the private metatable and the raw code. Tests: test_exhaustive.lua:162-185, test_sequential_hardening.lua:35-39. Not covered: ANDn/ORn arity below 2 (gates.lua:528-530) and the CMOS internal-failure branch (:259 and the six like it) still raise position-prefixed strings (probed: "gates.lua:529: logic_gates: ANDn requires at least 2 inputs", error_code returns nil).

Errors are read-only (a proxy with __newindex that raises and a private field store) and the is_invalid_* predicates recognise an error by a private weak registry of genuine instances rather than by its metatable and a mutable code field; test cases: a table given the same metatable, a mutated genuine error, error_code on both.

threats.name: caller text reaching error messages
threats.rationale: A rejected caller string is rendered with %q and cut at 32 bytes, numbers with %d/%.17g, any other value by its type name only (gates.lua:107-118), and the parameter names are constants or "name[i]" with an integer. On a freshly raised error no caller __tostring runs, but the error is a mutable table: once a caller sets err.value to a table with __tostring, the %s formatter (gates.lua:96-97 and the three like it) runs that caller code (probed), which belongs to lua.error-object-forgery-and-mutation. Residual: the 32-byte cut is on bytes, so a multi-byte UTF-8 character can be split; %.17g and %d are locale-independent in Lua's C formatting only for the decimal point of %g under os.setlocale (a consumer that sets a locale can change the rendering); err.value is attacker-influenced text that consumers must treat as data.

threats.name: ANDn/ORn accept an unbounded vararg; Register at the cap is slow
threats.rationale: ANDn and ORn call table.pack(...) on whatever the caller passes (gates.lua:527, :547) and loop one CMOS evaluation per input with no cap, so cost and memory grow linearly with a caller-chosen count; Lua limits a call to roughly one million values, and the package's own table.pack at gates.lua:527 raises an uncoded "stack overflow" at about 900,000 arguments (probed), the failure the cap and arity fix must code. threats.name: globals looked up at call time (error, tostring, table.pack, ipairs, string.format)
threats.rationale: Only a few standard functions are captured into locals at load (gates.lua:88-89: type, math.type, string.format, string.sub, select, setmetatable, getmetatable, rawget). Others are read from _G on every call: error (gates.lua:170, :175, :192, :201, :260, :297, :321, :351, :378, :406, :433, :529, :549), tostring (:260 and six like it), table.pack (:527, :547), ipairs (sequential.lua:77), and string.format reached through the string table (sequential.lua:64, :436). Confirmed by probe on Lua 5.5.0: after `_G.error = function() end`, pcall(lg.AND, "x", 1) returned true, nil, so validate_bit no longer rejects: the validator fails OPEN and the gate goes on to compute on a non-bit. Code that can write _G can do this at any time. Fix: capture every one of them into a local at load time and test replacing the globals afterwards. That is the part of the module-mutation class that the package controls; a caller that owns the VM can still alter upvalues with debug.setupvalue.
